content.value_statement: Technical SEO issues can block crawling, indexing, and page performance. This skill guides evidence-based audits with scorecards, prioritized fixes, and migration checks.
actual_capabilities: Reviews crawlability, robots.txt, sitemaps, redirect chains, and crawl waste.
Checks indexability signals, including noindex tags, X-Robots headers, canonicals, and duplicate clusters.
Assesses Core Web Vitals, mobile usability, HTTPS status, mixed content, and security headers.
Guides pre-migration audits with baseline snapshots, redirect maps, staging QA, and post-launch checks.
Creates scorecards, priority queues, fix roadmaps, and handoff summaries for technical SEO work.
limitations: It needs URLs, exports, crawl data, or user-provided reports to produce measured findings.
It cannot prove private analytics, Search Console, or paid tool data without user access.
JavaScript-rendered pages may need rendered DOM evidence before final schema or content conclusions.
Live index-push or write actions require explicit user approval and valid site ownership tokens.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Crawl and Indexing Loss
use_cases.description: Find robots.txt, noindex, canonical, sitemap, redirect, and status-code issues that block important pages.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Site Migration
use_cases.description: Build a migration risk map, redirect checklist, staging QA plan, and post-launch monitoring schedule.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Performance Fixes
use_cases.description: Review Core Web Vitals and related technical blockers, then rank fixes by search and business impact.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a technical SEO audit for this domain: [domain]. Focus on crawlability, indexability, Core Web Vitals, and HTTPS.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Issue Area
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for a known problem.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit crawlability and indexability for [domain]. Use robots.txt, sitemap, status codes, noindex, canonicals, and redirect evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Many URLs
prompt_templates.scenario: Bulk review for repeated page templates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Bulk audit these URL patterns: [list or sitemap]. Group pages by template, sample representative URLs, and report pattern-level fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration and launch risk review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pre-migration technical SEO audit for [old site] moving to [new site]. Include baselines, redirect mapping, staging QA, and post-launch checks.

output_examples.input: Audit the technical SEO of a SaaS website before a redesign.
output: A scorecard covering crawlability, indexability, performance, mobile, HTTPS, URL structure, schema, and international SEO.
A priority queue that separates launch blockers from improvements and hygiene tasks.
A handoff summary with evidence sources, open questions, and retest dates.

output_examples.input: Review a sitemap where many product pages are not indexed.
output: Grouped findings by product, category, blog, and landing page templates.
Pattern-level causes such as noindex rules, canonical conflicts, and sitemap pollution.
A compact fix plan ranked by affected page count and business impact.

output_examples.input: Prepare technical SEO checks for a domain migration.
output: A migration risk map, redirect coverage checklist, staging QA plan, and cutover checks.
Post-launch monitoring triggers for redirects, crawl errors, rankings, and traffic drops.

best_practices: Provide target URLs, sitemap links, crawl exports, and dates for every audit request.
Separate measured evidence from user-provided data and model estimates.
Retest high-priority fixes after deployment and record before-and-after evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not treat example domains, placeholders, or templates as measured audit facts.
Do not report JavaScript-rendered schema as missing until rendered DOM evidence is checked.
Do not run live submission or index-push actions without explicit user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits crawlability, indexability, Core Web Vitals, mobile usability, HTTPS, URL structure, structured data, and migration risks.

faq.question: Does it replace Search Console or crawler tools?
faq.answer: No. It organizes evidence from those tools and turns the findings into priorities and fixes.

faq.question: Can it audit large sites?
faq.answer: Yes. It can group many URLs by template, sample representative pages, and report pattern-level issues.

faq.question: Can it help before a migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports baselines, risk mapping, redirect planning, staging QA, cutover checks, and post-launch monitoring.

faq.question: How should evidence be labeled?
faq.answer: Evidence should be labeled as measured, user-provided, or estimated. Missing metrics should be marked as not available.

faq.question: Does it run live changes automatically?
faq.answer: No. Live submission or write actions should only happen after explicit user approval and ownership verification.
